## OPERATOR RULING 2026-09-21 — proceed as registered, ambiguity accepted

Put to the operator before any spend: rule 3's below 0.935 -> STOP branch is no longer self-interpreting. E - D = +0.010 established that the T117 bundle is worth a deficit-sized amount at res 224, and the bundle has never run at 384.

So this fold moves the corpus AND the resolution against a reference (C' 0.939) measured with neither, and a low score cannot distinguish "the input path did not help" from "384 is worse for our recipe".

The alternative offered was one extra cycle first — the bundle at 384 on the existing 44-slot corpus, directly comparable to B (0.929) and C' (0.939) at the same decode key, which would have made this rule's STOP branch readable.
The operator chose to proceed as registered. Recorded here so that a STOP outcome is read as what was knowingly accepted, not as a surprise.
Rules 1-5 and the 0.933-0.940 prediction are unchanged and not renegotiated.
If the fold lands below 0.935, the re-derivation rule 3 orders has the bundle-at-384 control as its first candidate, and this paragraph is the reason why.

T121 US-002: every training study through dicom_bag.make_bag, into one corpus.
WHAT IT WRITES, and why it is 148 GB and not the 49.4 GB T121 registered.
make_bag returns images of shape (N, 3, 384, 384) -- PRE-FORMED TRIPLETS, not a 76-slice single-channel volume.
T121's cost table assumed the latter.
Measured before this was written: windows inside a slot do NOT generally overlap (w0[1] != w1[0] for slots 1-4;
only slot 5 does), so they are STRIDED across the slot's span, the triplets are ATOMIC, and no compact slice volume can reconstruct them. 4,407 x 76 x 3 x 384^2 = 148.2 GB.
LAYOUT.
One fixed (76, 3, 384, 384) uint8 block per study, windows placed at their slot's offset, plus a (76,) uint8 validity mask.

The budgets (20,12,12,8,16,8) are dicom_bag.SLOT_BUDGETS and the offsets are their cumulative sum, so a window's slot is recoverable from its index alone -- which is what the T119 window rule needs and what the 0942's all-ones mask destroys.
WORKERS WRITE THEIR OWN ROW.
Each opens the memmap r+ and writes only its study's slice, so the rows never overlap and nothing is pickled back through the pool.
Returning 11 MB of pixels per study through IPC would move 148 GB through a pipe to write 148 GB to disk.
.venv/bin/python scripts/t121/materialise.py --out /mnt/S/rsna-corpus-dicombag
_dense_coat_specs allocates to this target.
Read from the notebook at run time rather than trusted here -- see assert_dense_target.
noqa: BLE001 -- categorised, never swallowed
vols is never touched.
Only the two arrays the head needs and the first pass threw away.
CONTIGUOUS, with the slot id kept per window.
The dense quotas vary per study, so no fixed per-slot region packs them;
storing the ids instead keeps the group boundaries the T119 rule needs, which the 0942's own all-ones mask throws away.
group by slot, stable within
never silently truncate the geometry
str keys: pyarrow refuses a dict column with int keys, and this frame is written to parquet at the end of a 30-minute pass.

THE DENSE ALLOCATION DOES NOT FIT THE FIXED OFFSET LAYOUT, and that is a fact about the allocator rather than an implementation gap: quotas vary per study, so slot 1 may take 30 windows in one study and 12 in another.
A fixed per-slot region would have to be sized for the worst case in every slot and would not pack.

The dense corpus therefore stores windows CONTIGUOUSLY with a per-window slot id, which is strictly more informative -- the group boundaries the T119 rule needs are recoverable from the ids, where the 0942's own all-ones mask destroys them.
the notebook's dense target is {_m.group(1) if _m else 'unreadable'}, not {DENSE_TARGET}.
The corpus would be built to a budget the kernel no longer uses, which trains an arm on one distribution and serves it another -- the exact failure this variant exists to close.
Re-read the allocator.
--sidecar-only refuses --limit.

The sidecars are indexed by the SAME row as the corpus, so a partial pass writes arrays that are shorter than vols.npy and silently misalign every study past the limit -- the trainer would read one study's depth against another's pixels.
--sidecar-only needs an existing corpus at {out}
REFUSING: {nbytes/1e9:.1f} GB needed, {free/1e9:.1f} GB free at {out}.
A half-written corpus is worse than none -- the trainer would read zeros as real pixels with a mask that says they are valid.
NOTHING BELONGING TO THE EXISTING CORPUS IS OPENED "w+".

An earlier version of this branch fell through to the allocation below, which opens masks.npy with mode="w+" -- that ZEROES the validity mask of a 148 GB corpus a fold may be reading, and every study would then look like it had no valid windows.
The sidecars were allocated above and vols/masks/ids are left exactly as they are.
T121 US-003: peak VRAM at res 384 WITH the SWA fp32 copy resident.
WHY MEASURED AND NOT READ OFF A TABLE.
T121 rule 4 warns that "the SWA holds a 0.27 GiB fp32 copy in VRAM from epoch 13 that calib_4070.py never measured, and 384/bs2 is 97% full with it" -- and then says "profile before launching;
do not assume the table." A fold that OOMs at epoch 13 of 16 has burned ~7 h to produce nothing, and it would do it in the tail, where the SWA copy appears.

So this runs the REAL objects: the real CoatMIL at the real res, a real forward and backward over a real bag shape, gradient accumulation as the recipe uses it, and an SWA accumulator materialised as fp32 on the card.
It reports the peak, not an estimate, and it reports the largest (bs, accum) that fits with headroom or says that none does.
.venv/bin/python scripts/t121/profile_vram.py --res 384 --k 12
no CUDA device;
this measurement is about a real card
channels_last is applied to the MODEL only.
The bag is rank 5 and channels_last is a rank-4 format;
CoatMIL.encode flattens (b, k) and applies it to the window batch itself, which is what the conv stages see.
Applying it to the 5D input here raises, and the first version of this script did exactly that.
THE SWA COPY, resident, as it is from the first tail epoch onward.
noqa: F841
